explanation: Passing an electric current through water splits it into hydrogen and oxygen gas, with exactly twice as much hydrogen collected as oxygen.

beaker_view.initial_appearance: Colourless water, with two electrodes dipped in and connected to a power source.
beaker_view.final_appearance: Still colourless; gas has simply collected above each electrode.
beaker_view.observation: A steady stream of small bubbles rises from each electrode, with noticeably more gas collecting above one electrode (hydrogen) than the other (oxygen), in a 2:1 ratio.
